items.title: Bobby Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: written by Earl Hines and Walter Thor

ctx.x: Well here’s a hard question. When you’re improvising, can you describe to me what’s going on in your head?

Well if you’re playing a tune, say like “Rosetta” or something like that, written by Earl Hines and Walter Thor, I play the melody if I’m playing by myself, I play the melody the first chorus. I try to remember the melody, I try to play the melody most of the time on the first chorus. And then I would change into a jazz chorus and I would think ahead of time in my head, which chord progressions are coming up next. I know F is coming here and D7 is coming there and G7 is coming there — I have it all stored in my…
Do you think that there are Bobby Gordon licks?
